title: Exploring Diffusion Transformer Designs via Grafting

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Abstract states: 'all tested hybrid designs achieve excellent quality (FID: 2.15–2.38 vs. 2.27 for DiT-XL/2) ... demonstrating that grafting consistently outperforms the baseline across all replacement ratios and operator types.' The FID value 2.15 appears nowhere in the paper's results (Tables 1-6, Figs. 4); the actual range of successful hybrids spans 2.38 (MLP r=6) to 2.64/2.74 (Tab. 4), and the Conclusion itself states 'competitive quality (FID 2.38–2.64 vs. 2.27 baseline)'. The claim 'consistently outperforms the baseline across all replacement ratios' is contradicted by Tab. 4 (e.g., Hyena-SE 100% FID 8.23, Hyena-X 75% FID 3.69, SWA 75% FID 3.09).

Section 3.4 text: 'for k=32, all 28 layers exhibit L_k > 0.7, with 22 layers exceeding 0.85'. Figure 2 caption: 'At k=32, 15 out of 28 layers exhibit values exceeding 0.5'. Both describe the same k=32 statistic over the same 28 MHA operators and are mutually exclusive ('all 28 layers > 0.7' vs 'only 15 of 28 layers > 0.5').

Section 6 states: 'our grafted model surpasses even the original DiT-XL/2 (FID=2.27) when evaluated on a held-out test set' and the intro Result claims it 'substantially outperforms all baseline models regardless of depth or parameter count'. Table 6 reports the grafted model's FID as 2.77, which is WORSE (higher) than DiT-XL/2's 2.27 (and also worse than TinyDiT-D14 w/ MKD is not applicable, but DiT-XL/2 2.27 < 2.77). The claim reverses the direction of the evidence.

Section 3.3 text: 'using just 10% of the training data (128k samples), we achieve an FID of 2.53 vs. 2.27 for the baseline' (referring to MHA full self-grafting). Table 2 reports MHA full self-grafting with 10% data as FID 2.49, and Table 4 'Self-grafting 100%' also reports 2.49. The value 2.53 in the text corresponds to the MLP r=3 (50%) row, not MHA self-grafting.

Section 4.2 text: 'At 100% replacement, performance sharply degrades (all FIDs > 75)'. Table 4 lists Hyena-SE 100% with an actual FID of 8.23 (not >75), and the Table 4 footnote defines the ✗ marker as 'FID > 50', while Fig. 4(b) states 'Full (100%) FID > 140'. Three mutually inconsistent thresholds (50 / 75 / 140) are used for the same 100%-replacement condition, and the blanket 'all FIDs > 75' is false.

Abstract, Intro Result II, Section 5 and the Table 5 caption all report a '1.43× speedup' for the 50%-grafted PixArt-Σ model (whose GenEval is quoted as 47.78 vs 49.75). Table 5's own data for that model list Latency 148.32 ms (1.59×) and Throughput 13.48 img/s (1.59×); 235.46/148.32 = 1.59, not 1.43. The 1.43× figure does not appear in any results table.

Conclusion: 'grafting completely solves the problem of architecture design for diffusion transformers, eliminating the need for costly pretraining' and 'grafting universally outperforms training from scratch across all tasks, modalities, and model scales'. Limitations (Supp. I): 'it remains an open question whether architectures that perform well under grafting also perform well when trained from scratch.' No from-scratch training of any hybrid design is reported anywhere in the paper, so the 'universally outperforms training from scratch' claim is unsupported and contradicts the stated open question.

Table 6 caption defines 'A.R. (Aspect Ratio) is defined as model width divided by depth (e.g., 1152/14 = 82.3)'. The Grafting (Ours) rows report A.R. = 164.6 at depth 14 with the same hidden width as DiT-XL/2 (1152), for which the stated definition gives 1152/14 = 82.3. A.R. 164.6 would require width 2304, which is inconsistent with the +6% parameter change (675M -> 712M) and with the caption's own definition.

Section 5: 'Hyena-X was chosen based on its good quality-efficiency tradeoff in the ImageNet-1K setup, achieving FID 2.61 with 20% data (see Fig. 4(b))'. The 20%-data FID 2.61 for Hyena-X appears in Fig. 4(a) (data-scaling ablation); Fig. 4(b) shows layer-selection heuristics and contains no 20%-data result. Wrong figure cross-reference.

summary: Verification run in uncertainty mode (escalation threshold 0.30, strictness lenient). The paper was segmented into 74 typed snippets (27 sections, 5 equations, 16 tables, 26 figures); all were triaged, and 20 high-uncertainty snippets were escalated to specialist verifiers (text, statistical, math) plus a full-paper cross-section consistency pass. Nine findings, four of them high-confidence (>= 0.85): (1) the Abstract's FID range '2.15-2.38' matches no reported result (successful hybrids actually span 2.38-2.74; Conclusion says 2.38-2.64) and its claim that grafting 'consistently outperforms the baseline across all replacement ratios' is contradicted by Table 4; (2) Figure 2's caption ('15 of 28 layers exceed 0.5') directly contradicts Section 3.4 ('all 28 layers have L_k > 0.7, 22 exceeding 0.85'); (3) Section 6 claims the grafted model 'surpasses even the original DiT-XL/2 (FID=2.27)' while Table 6 reports its FID as 2.77 (worse); (4) Section 3.3 reports MHA full self-grafting FID 2.53 vs 2.49 in Tables 2/4. Additional medium-confidence findings: 'all FIDs > 75' at 100% replacement conflicts with Hyena-SE 100% FID 8.23 and the paper's own inconsistent FID>50 / FID>140 thresholds; the 1.43x speedup cited in text/captions is 1.59x in Table 5; the Conclusion's 'universally outperforms training from scratch' contradicts the Limitations' stated open question; Table 6 A.R. 164.6 is inconsistent with the width/depth definition (1152/14=82.3); and a Fig. 4(b) cross-reference should be Fig. 4(a). Equations and FLOP formulas were checked and no provable algebraic errors found. Verdict: NEEDS_CORRECTION.
